note: Directed prerequisite edges between misconceptions. An edge A -> B means: you cannot reliably repair B until A is solid, so a miss on B while A is still open should be routed backward to A first. Edges are authored, not inferred: a real dependency is one where the downstream reasoning is impossible without the upstream fact, not merely one where the topics are adjacent.

edges.why: Ordering only matters once you know evaluation stops at the first match. Without that, 'specific before general' is an arbitrary rule to memorise.
You cannot judge whether a rule is too broad until you can read which side holds the service port and which direction it is written in.
Zone direction is an argument about which side initiates. That is unreadable without source and destination being solid first.
Return traffic is the reverse of a flow you must already be able to write.
A signature is a hash encrypted with a private key. If hashing and encryption are still blurred, the properties a signature does and does not provide cannot be derived.
Salting is a property of hashing. It cannot be reasoned about while hashing is still confused with encryption.
Revocation checking is about trusting a signed statement from the CA. The signature properties come first.
Every access control model is an authorization model. Picking between them is impossible while authorization is still conflated with authentication.
Factors are an authentication concept. Counting them only makes sense once authentication is cleanly separated.
Least privilege and need to know are applied through an access control model. The model has to be solid first.
Deterrent and preventive are both control TYPES. Separating them is pointless while the type axis is still being confused with the category axis.
Same axis problem. Both are types, and the common error is answering on the wrong axis entirely.
This is the identical two-axis trap in a different domain. Fixing the pattern once makes the second instance much cheaper.
Deciding to mitigate, transfer, accept or avoid is an economic judgement against the annualised loss. Without ALE the decision has no basis.
The BIA is identified by its outputs. If RTO and RPO are still swapped, the thing that distinguishes a BIA from a risk assessment is invisible.
Quantitative analysis IS the SLE/ARO/ALE calculation. The distinction is empty until those are solid.
The choice is only forced once you know containment precedes eradication. Out of phase order, powering off looks like a reasonable first move.
Choosing a network control over patching or scanning is a phase decision before it is a technology decision.
Reimaging is eradication. Its timing relative to containment and evidence collection is what makes it right or wrong.
Collection order only matters if the machine is still running. The decision not to power it off comes first.
Why containment must be a network control follows directly from the malware propagating by itself. Get the propagation model right and the containment choice falls out.
Scoping is the analysis phase. Without the phases, there is no stage at which scope is the question being asked.
EAP methods only exist inside Enterprise mode. Choosing one before the mode distinction is solid is answering a question that has not been reached.
RADIUS enters the picture because Enterprise delegates the decision. That is the reason to know which AAA protocol applies.
Understanding that WPA protects data frames but not management frames depends on knowing what the WPA handshake actually covers.
Guest design starts from the fact that no per-user identity exists, which is the Personal versus Enterprise distinction.
Failure mode is only a live question for a device that sits inline. Inline versus out of band comes first.
Degrees of separation are judged against what a controlled connection actually permits, which is the zone direction argument.
The reason zero-day matters is that no patch exists, so you must reach for a compensating control. Without that concept the distinction has no consequence.
Supply chain compromise is defined by nothing being exploited at all. That only reads as surprising once exploitation of a known or unknown flaw is clear.
Collision and birthday attack the hash; downgrade attacks the negotiation. Separating them needs hashing and encryption already separated.
Telling live interception from a replayed capture is a mechanism-versus-outcome distinction, the same discipline the application attack family demands.
Review types are ranked by independence, which is the same before-versus-ongoing, who-is-accountable reasoning as diligence versus care.
Choosing between a questionnaire, a SOC 2 and a right-to-audit clause is a judgement about independence, which the audit types establish.
A right-to-audit clause is a contract term. It cannot be selected without knowing what the agreement types do.
The governance hierarchy is another specificity ladder, and the failure mode is identical: answering at the wrong level.
Behavioural detection matters precisely because there is no signature yet. The zero-day concept is what gives EDR its reason to exist.
The answer to ransomware is a restorable backup. If replication is still mistaken for backup, paying starts to look rational.
Hot, warm and cold are selected against an RTO. Without the target the three are just degrees of expense.
Backup frequency is set by the RPO. Choosing between snapshot, replication and journaling is choosing a recovery point.
Availability design sits on top of the recovery site decision.
Reading authentication logs for a pattern starts with being able to read the simplest pattern: many failures on one account versus one failure on many.
The application attack family is separated by mechanism. SQLi versus XSS is the cheapest instance of that discipline and the one the exam uses most.
